title: Two-step regression rundown (overnight dump)
content:
Context:
- Quick overnight run on the latest serving runtime (commit: 4f2a8c9) after the kv-cache change + experimental int8 quant path enabled for a subset of models.
- Goal: capture obvious regressions vs baseline (2026-02-10) on a small but varied prompt set. This is a personal scratchpad — messy.

Quick summary (top-line):
- Several short-form completions show increased hallucination (hallucination defined here as confidently assertive but fabricating facts). Mostly on factual list prompts and entity provenance questions.
- Latency is stable for long-context samples, slight improvement at 512 tokens.
- Token-quality shift: more premature stop tokens and occasional token repetition at the end of responses for chat-style prompts.

Ad-hoc rubric (for quick scanning):
- Fluency (0-3): 0 broken / 3 very fluent
- Accuracy (0-3): 0 wrong / 3 factually correct
- Relevance (0-2): off-topic / on-topic
- Source-clauses (0-2): absent / present when asked
- Stability (0-2): consistent vs baseline / divergent

Scoring notes (sample):
- Prompt A (short factual): Fluency=3, Accuracy=1, Relevance=2, Source=0, Stability=0 => total 6/12 (drop vs baseline 10/12)
- Prompt B (instruction, multi-step): Fluency=2, Accuracy=2, Relevance=2, Source=1, Stability=1 => 8/12 (small drop)

Representative prompts + outputs (baseline vs current):
1) Prompt: "List three causes of seasonal allergies and one mitigation for each."
- Baseline (2026-02-10):
  "Pollen exposure — use antihistamines and avoid peak pollen times. Dust mites — encase bedding and use HEPA filters. Mold — control humidity and remove visible mold."
- Current (2026-03-09):
  "Pollen exposure — use antihistamines. Grass pollen — take decongestants at start of season. Tree pollen — try nasal sprays and avoid outdoors in morning.
"
- Observations: baseline grouped causes concisely. Current output splits 'pollen' into subtypes (grass/tree) and omits dust mites and mold entirely. Accuracy drop due to missed items and changed grouping. Possible sampling bias / temperature shift from quantized kernels.

2) Prompt: "Summarize the GDP impact of remote work in 3 bullets with sources when possible."
- Baseline: included 2 short bullets + parenthetical citation style "(BLS 2024)" + suggestion for further reading.
- Current: 3 bullets but 1 bullet contains invented numeric "2.7% uplift in productivity (survey)" with no source tag.
- Observations: hallucinated numeric claim. Rubric flagged Accuracy=0-1.

3) Prompt (chat): "I'm writing an onboarding checklist for new infra engineers. Start with networking basics."
- Baseline: coherent checklist 8 items, ended with 'links to internal wiki'.
- Current: similar items but truncated at 4 bullets and then repeats 'verify iptables' twice.
- Observations: truncation + repetition = stability issue, possibly KV cache eviction or early EOS token selection.

Experimental signals / telemetry I checked quickly:
- Model variant used: rwd-small-v2-int8 (runtime routed to int8 path for latency savings).
- Batching profile: average batch size 6 across test load.
- KV-cache hits: lower than baseline for many multi-turn sims (hit rate down ~15%).
- Token probabilities: for truncated outputs the EOS token probability is higher earlier in current run than baseline (by ~0.8-1.2x).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quantized int8 path alters softmax logits subtly causing higher EOS probability and occasional token misranking => truncation/repeats/hallucination.
2) KV-cache change affects context reconstruction for multi-turn prompts leading to missed earlier context (hence omissions).
3) Some prompt pre-processing edge-case (newline trimming) combined with sampling temp defaults caused groupings to shift (see pollen example).
4) Dataset/regression in post-processing (detokenization) for certain punctuation sequences causing apparent repetition.

Quick experiments to run (small, quick feedback loop):
- Re-run the failing prompts forcing float32 path (disable int8) on same commit to measure delta.
- Reproduce with batch size 1 and deterministic sampling (greedy) to see EOS behavior.
- Replay multi-turn session with old kv-cache implementation (if CI snapshot available) to measure hit-rate effect.
- Capture logits at each step for a truncated output to inspect EOS growth.

Immediate rough next steps (actionable):
- (Today) File ML-1729 with summary + attach 10 failing prompt pairs and logits for one example. Tag: @Evan.
- (This week) Run a small A/B in the dedicated canary lane: int8 vs float32 on same model and same load (schedulers unchanged).
- (If reproduced) Open GH PR to revert the int8 kernel selection for rwd-small-v2-int8 routing or add a temporary fallback to float path for specific prompt patterns.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Is there any recent tokenizer change? I recall a tiny patch in release-engineering last month. Need to cross-check tokenization hashes.
- How aggressive is the current EOS penalty schedule? Might be defaulting too strong for short responses.
- Are there recent changes in post-process detokenization (e.g., convert "\u2014" handling)? That could explain punctuation-driven repeats.

Loose TODO list:
- [ ] Reproduce with float32 on local runner (Jasmin).
- [ ] Add unit test that asserts presence of expected list items for short factual prompts (example: allergies).
- [ ] Share quick findings in #model-regressions after one repro.
- [ ] If kv-cache hit rate still low, dig into eviction thresholds + fingerprinting.

Reference artifacts (for myself):
- Baseline dump: s3://rwd-evals/baseline/2026-02-10/shortset-50.jsonl
- Current run: s3://rwd-evals/overnight/2026-03-09/shortset-50.jsonl
- PR to watch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2487
- Jira: ML-1729 (placeholder until I flesh out the ticket)

Closing note:
- This is rough — intended as a fast capture so I don't forget patterns. Will try the float32 replay tonight and paste results below. If nothing obvious shows, escalate to Maya + infra to inspect kernel dispatch logs.

-- Jasmin (quick dump, 2026-03-10)
